idea: Four descriptive checks from 5.4 the assistant can run before trusting t-tests/CIs on per-seed or per-vehicle KPIs: (1) histogram shape, (2) share of values within 1, 2, 3 s of the mean vs 68/95/100 percent, (3) IQR/s close to 1.3, (4) normal probability plot (correlation of ordered data with normal quantiles). If failed, route to nonparametric_test or a transform.
does: Reports the checks and a verdict that selects parametric or nonparametric comparison
notes: Pairs with distribution_shape (SRC_020) and nonparametric_test; cheap guard for run_experiment output.

idea: Plan the experiment before running it: sample size for a CI half-width n=(z*sigma/SE)^2 (7.5), for a difference of means n1=n2=z^2(s1^2+s2^2)/SE^2 and of proportions (9.5; use p=0.5 conservatively), paired-difference version n=(z*sd_d/SE)^2, and power 1-beta for a given true shift (8.7: border x0=mu0+z*sigma/sqrt(n), beta=P(z<(x0-mua)/se)). In ACMS a pilot of 3 to 5 seeds gives sigma; the tool answers how many seeds detect an X% change in delay, the minimum detectable effect of a 20-seed experiment, and a power curve over effect size. acms_tools.md lists 'no statistical power analysis' as not built.
does: Seeds needed and minimum detectable effect for paired or independent comparisons, with power curve
inputs: pilot SD (or run id/experiment id), effect size or half-width, alpha, power, paired flag
outputs: seeds required, power at current seeds, minimum detectable difference, curve points
existing: partial: run_experiment (replications needed for a precision only)
notes: Use t quantiles not z for small n (iterate). Directly listed as not built. Feed into note_plan so the agent states expected power before testing.

topic: Omnibus ANOVA and ranking of all scenarios
idea: For k scenarios run with independent seeds (completely randomized design): one-way ANOVA table (SST, SSE, F=MST/MSE, Table 10.4-10.5) then, if F is significant, all c=k(k-1)/2 pairwise CIs with an experimentwise error rate by Tukey (equal n), Bonferroni or Scheffe (contrasts), summarised as a ranked list of means with lines joining the groups that do not differ (Fig 10.17). run_experiment compares each scenario only against the baseline; this ranks all designs against each other and says which are tied.
does: ANOVA F, Tukey/Bonferroni all-pairs CIs and group letters for scenarios on a KPI
outputs: ANOVA table, pairwise CIs, ranking with tie groups, best scenario set
existing: partial: run_experiment (paired t vs baseline, Bonferroni)
notes: Tukey needs the studentized-range quantile (numerical integration, pure Python) else use Bonferroni. Book: ANOVA is robust to non-normality but not to unequal variances (use equal n); fall back to Kruskal-Wallis.

topic: Randomized block ANOVA with seeds as blocks
idea: Randomized block design (10.4): each seed is a block containing every scenario; SS(Total)=SST+SSB+SSE with df (b-1)(k-1) for error; F tests treatments after removing seed-to-seed variation, and the F for blocks tells whether common random numbers/pairing paid off (SSB large). For k=2, F=t^2 equals the paired t test (shown in the book). Extends the paired t to k>2 scenarios with a single omnibus test and blocking-efficiency report.
does: Two-way ANOVA with seeds as blocks and scenarios as treatments; reports whether pairing reduced error
outputs: ANOVA table with treatment and block rows, F, p, blocking benefit ratio
notes: Pair with Tukey on block-adjusted means (MSE with (b-1)(k-1) df). Same data shape run_experiment already holds.

idea: Interpretation order for a two-factor factorial (procedure box, 10.5): F test of treatment means first; if significant partition into interaction and main effects; test interaction before main effects; if interaction significant do NOT interpret main effects alone, compare cell means by multiple comparisons; if only main effects, compare level means; if the treatment F is non-significant add replications or factors. Encode as the assistant's rule for explaining factorial_experiment output (e.g. a TSP effect that depends on demand level).
does: Decision procedure and plain-language verdict for factorial ANOVA results
outputs: ordered findings with warnings about interaction
notes: Companion to SRC_032 factorial_experiment idea; prompt/rule text rather than code.

topic: Prediction versus confidence interval in regress
idea: Add a predict mode to regress: at a new x_p give y_hat with the CI for the mean response (y_hat +/- t*s*sqrt(1/n+(x_p-xbar)^2/SSxx)) and the wider prediction interval for a single new run (with the extra 1 under the root), and flag extrapolation outside the fitted x range (12.12 pitfall). Answers what delay at 130% demand, with an interval for the mean and for the next seed.
does: Mean and individual prediction intervals at chosen x, with extrapolation warning
inputs: regress inputs plus x values to predict
outputs: y_hat, CI mean, prediction interval, extrapolation flag
existing: partial: regress (coefficients, t, R2, F only)
notes: Multiple-regression form needs (X'X)^-1 (already needed for SRC_020 regress_diagnostics).

topic: Residual-plot rules and nested model F test
idea: Residual checks 12.11: residuals vs y_hat for non-constant variance (cone shape) with ln(y), sqrt(y) or arcsin sqrt(y) as variance-stabilising fixes, regression outlier rule |residual|>3s, histogram/normal plot of residuals; nested-model F test (12.9) F=[(SSE_R-SSE_C)/(g)]/[SSE_C/(n-k-1)] to decide whether interaction/quadratic/dummy terms add value; quadratic and interaction model forms (12.5-12.6).
does: Reports residual diagnostics and compares nested models by F
inputs: regress inputs, reduced and complete term sets
outputs: outlier rows, variance pattern verdict, nested F and p
notes: Overlaps regress_terms/regress_diagnostics from SRC_020; implement as one regress upgrade.
